final_candidate.title: Receipt-Carried Epochs for Strict Framework-Native FPGA Inference
final_candidate.hook: On the unchanged Gemma 3 1B F16 graph, the same accepted-node sequence can reduce pp512 launches from 224,936 to at most 1,626 and tg128 launches from 202,530 to at most 104,877 while retaining byte-identical observable tensors under deterministic kernel execution. The surprising test is whether that launch-count collapse also lowers full-path wall clock, rather than merely moving wait time elsewhere.
final_candidate.hook_shape_rationale: Shape (a) passes because the named launch-count and full-path wall-clock metrics predict a large pp512/tg128 reduction while the support trace and observable outputs remain fixed, a live-runtime result not established by the closest replay study. Shape (b) was considered but rejected because transition-aware dispatch already names transition costs, so describing admission/execution coupling as merely tacit would overstate the reframe.

gap_closure.gap: No retrieved frontier leaf establishes that a framework-native backend can retain exact support decisions, explicit failure behavior, tensor-state continuity, and accelerator-artifact identity while execution no longer incurs one host-visible completion cycle per admitted unit — stakes: backend maintainers otherwise face either silent semantic drift and wrong outputs or a formally correct integration whose launch overhead blocks useful deployment and wastes FPGA development effort.
gap_closure.how_closed: Closed by replacing per-tile XRT launches and per-node waits with a finite vector-descriptor operator ABI plus receipt-carried graph epochs; corpus support is thin in this domain, and C12's closest exemplars concern structural plumbing in other staged systems.

gap_closure.gap: No retrieved frontier leaf demonstrates on live hardware that reducing transition and synchronization amplification across a complete autoregressive run preserves the connected model's outputs and costs once dispatcher, framework, state-management, and failure paths are included — stakes: edge-LLM practitioners can spend most runtime in control overhead despite accelerating accepted operators, while replay-only conclusions may not transfer to deployed heterogeneous runtimes.
gap_closure.how_closed: Closed by a matched real-GGML evaluation that holds prompts, graph inputs, clocks, model, board, and application path fixed, compares the baseline with the complete receipt-epoch mechanism, and uses descriptor-unpacked and per-call-wait ablations to separate launch packing from commit timing while independently checking launches, downstream wall clock, output/state equivalence, support decisions, within-arm receipt-to-artifact identity, and zero fallback; corpus support is thin for FPGA runtimes, with the closest C02 exemplars drawn from other evaluation domains.

final_candidate.core_mechanism: The shared evaluation object is a paired execution ledger for one unchanged `ggml_backend_graph_compute` invocation of Gemma 3 1B F16: baseline and candidate runs record the same ordered admitted calls, support outcomes, artifact identifiers, tensor versions, errors, XRT starts, waits, and final observable tensors. For admitted call i, the backend creates an immutable receipt R_i = (operator family, dtype/shape signature, support-predicate version, input/output tensor IDs and versions, mutable-state read/write set, xclbin UUID, kernel name, kernel-ABI digest); every field comes from the actual GGML node, backend tensor metadata, and loaded XRT artifact, so no oracle or learned quantity is used. Before execution, a strict preflight requires one matching R_i for every graph node, rejects a stale artifact or changed signature explicitly, and has no CPU branch. Each accepted operator artifact receives a finite vector-descriptor ABI: its descriptor array is the existing ordered list of tile arguments formerly sent through K_i separate `xrt::run` starts, and one terminating launch loops over exactly those K_i descriptors in the original arithmetic order before returning, without combining different GGML operators. Calls are then submitted asynchronously in graph order, while a device-visible tensor-version table gates each finite operator wrapper on its receipts' input versions and publishes output versions; the framework observes completion only at the graph epoch boundary, defined as return from that graph-compute invocation or an earlier explicit synchronize/copy/read request. Stateful writes such as KV-cache updates target copy-on-write pages named by provisional versions, downstream operators read those provisional versions, and the epoch atomically advances the committed version table only after every run and receipt-status slot succeeds; on any validation, enqueue, or device fault it reports the first error, discards provisional versions, and never falls back. Artifact identity is preserved because a launch is legal only when R_i's xclbin UUID, kernel name, and ABI digest equal the loaded artifact, and tensor-state continuity is preserved by the version gates and commit rule rather than by a host wait after each call. The launch-amplification quantity is A = L/H, where H is the number of admitted GGML calls recorded at backend entry and L is the number of completed XRT run starts recorded by the XRT wrapper over the same full path; the construction makes L at most H for accepted execution, while synchronization count S is the number of blocking host completion calls and is one per graph epoch unless the unchanged application explicitly requests an earlier boundary. Under the stated assumptions that each vector wrapper preserves descriptor order, kernels are deterministic, and no tensor becomes host-visible before commit, observational equivalence means byte equality of every host-observed tensor and committed state plus equality of the ordered support, explicit-error, and artifact-identity traces. This is neither graph fusion nor capture, a persistent kernel, an FPGA instruction overlay, or dataflow compilation: operator boundaries and replaceable artifacts remain intact, every operator kernel terminates, and the only substituted slots are intra-operator launch expansion and host-visible completion placement. Across baseline and candidate arms, artifact identity means that the artifact actually launched equals the xclbin UUID, kernel name, and ABI digest admitted by that arm's receipt; installing the vector ABI intentionally changes the candidate artifact relative to the baseline, so cross-arm UUID or ABI equality is not claimed. Process-level H, L, and S are sums over all graph epochs, A is reported only when H > 0 (otherwise N/A), and commit at a graph boundary completes before `ggml_backend_graph_compute` returns.
final_candidate.core_mechanism_reasoning:
BLOCK 1 — PREMISES
P1: The measured pp512 and tg128 paths are control dominated: XRT wait is 96.25% and 79.58% of profiled operator time, respectively, so launch/wait amplification is a plausible end-to-end bottleneck.
P2: Existing accepted operator calls already materialize an ordered tile-argument list before issuing their many XRT runs; this is believed because the current dispatch expands 1,626 pp512 calls into 224,936 launches and 104,877 tg128 calls into 202,530 launches.
P3: A finite operator wrapper can consume that descriptor list in the same order without changing arithmetic; untested — falsification target, because hidden host-side effects between tile launches could invalidate packing.
P4: Device-resident tensor dependencies and mutable KV state can be represented by monotonically increasing tensor versions plus copy-on-write commit; this is believed from the backend's existing tensor storage ownership but remains implementation-sensitive to aliasing.
P5 observation-model: the instrumentation intercepts every accepted GGML backend entry, XRT run start, blocking completion, artifact lookup, and graph-return boundary on the named Gemma path; completeness is checked by reconciling each call with exactly one support receipt and each XRT event with a receipt, rather than assuming sampled profiler intervals are complete.
ESTIMAND: for the fixed Gemma 3 1B F16 U280 pp512 and tg128 processes, the target is the paired change in full-path wall clock from graph-compute entry to committed output availability, together with A = total completed XRT starts divided by total admitted GGML calls, across repeated executions of the same prompts, binaries, clocks, and application path.
BLOCK 2 — NAIVE-BASELINE AUDIT
Naive baseline: delete every per-launch or per-call `wait()` in the current backend, call `start()` in the existing order, and wait once when `ggml_backend_graph_compute` returns. Branch (i): this silently assumes command arguments, temporary tensors, aliased buffers, mutable KV state, artifact bindings, and delayed errors remain valid and correctly ordered without the waits, which is false for a strict stateful backend; receipt pinning, immutable descriptors, tensor-version gates, copy-on-write state, and first-fault commit confront that failure directly. The transaction machinery is a standard systems tool, but this instance is not solved by a generic transaction layer because GGML separates per-node support admission from graph execution while XRT binds finite runs to mutable buffer objects and replaceable xclbin/kernel ABIs, and stateful decode aliases tensors across epochs; the contribution is the domain-specific receipt/version contract spanning those three lifecycles.
BLOCK 3 — DESIGN RATIONALE
The two gaps share machinery because the receipt ledger that makes deferred completion strict also supplies the independent oracle for the matched live-hardware diagnostic; a separate benchmark subsystem would risk measuring a different path. I rejected host command capture/batching because it lands on the occupied CUDA-Graphs-like node, whole-graph fusion and StreamTensor/CODO-style compilation because they take graph ownership, persistent kernels and instruction overlays because they collapse artifact boundaries, and fully spatial streaming because it replaces the runtime contract. I also rejected wait elision alone because it cannot roll back KV state or bind a prior support decision to the artifact actually executed. ESTIMAND CLARIFICATION: in each paired pp512 or tg128 application trial, full-path wall clock runs from the first backend graph-compute entry to availability of the final committed output requested by the unchanged application, including all intervening graph epochs; per-epoch graph-entry-to-commit latency is reported only as a diagnostic, and H, L, and S are summed over those epochs.

2. Extend the support-query path to emit R_i records keyed by graph invocation and node index; inputs are the real node signature, backend tensor metadata, support-predicate version, and loaded xclbin/kernel metadata, and output is an immutable receipt table or an explicit unsupported result.
3. Add strict graph preflight before any FPGA work; input is the ordered GGML graph plus receipt table, and output is either a fully admitted epoch or the original explicit failure with zero XRT launches and no CPU execution.
4. Refactor each of the 11 accepted operator-family wrappers so its host code writes the existing ordered tile arguments into a descriptor BO and starts one finite vector-descriptor kernel; inputs are the unchanged tensors and tile list, and output is the same device tensor that feeds subsequent GGML nodes and ultimately the model logits.
5. Add receipt checks and tensor-version gates to each finite wrapper; inputs are R_i, descriptor BO, and device version table, and outputs are either the new output-tensor versions consumed by downstream operators or a first-fault status code.
6. Replace per-call waits with graph-ordered asynchronous submissions and retain every descriptor BO, run handle, and tensor allocation until epoch resolution; inputs are admitted calls and dependency versions, and output is an in-flight epoch whose downstream nodes consume only published producer versions.
7. Route KV-cache and other mutable writes to provisional copy-on-write pages and resolve aliases through the epoch version map; inputs are committed state and node write sets, and output is staged state read by later attention operations without changing generated logits before commit.
8. Implement epoch commit at graph return and at unchanged explicit synchronize/copy/read boundaries; inputs are all run statuses and provisional versions, and output is either atomically committed tensors/state returned to llama.cpp or an explicit first error with provisional state discarded.
9. Replay all 112 c64/c512 signatures and 2,422 accepted U280 dispatch observations against the baseline; inputs are the existing test corpus and exact artifacts, and outputs are bytewise tensor comparisons plus equality checks for support decisions, errors, artifact IDs, and absence of CPU fallback.
10. Run matched pp512 and tg128 Gemma campaigns with warmups and repeated trials, then run descriptor-unpacked and per-call-wait controls; inputs are identical prompts, clocks, F16 model, U280, and binaries except the named intervention, and outputs are A, blocking synchronization count, XRT wait time, full-path wall clock, logits/tokens, and strictness traces. For Step 3, each candidate wrapper ABI declares a finite per-signature descriptor-count and descriptor-byte capacity, and preflight verifies every K_i fits before any XRT launch. For Step 8, epoch resolution and commit complete before the corresponding graph-compute or explicit visibility request returns. For Step 9, artifact checks compare each receipt with the artifact actually loaded and launched within the same arm and record the intentional baseline-to-vector-wrapper mapping; they do not require baseline and candidate UUID/ABI equality.
final_candidate.falsification_prediction: Run unchanged llama.cpp with Gemma 3 1B F16 on the Alveo U280 for matched pp512 and tg128 trials, comparing the current strict backend, receipt epochs, receipt epochs with one descriptor per launch, and receipt epochs with per-call waits; measure launch count, A, full-path wall clock, outputs, committed KV state, support/error trace, artifact IDs, and fallback count. If the mechanism works, A and blocking waits decrease, and downstream pp512 and tg128 wall clock decreases while observable tensors/state and strictness traces remain equivalent and fallback remains zero. The single load-bearing variable is launch amplification A; the negative-control intervention disables descriptor packing while preserving receipts and versioned commit, and it should drive full-path wall clock back toward the current backend, while a per-call-wait control distinguishes launch reduction from synchronization deferral. Falsify the candidate on this existing path if launch reduction fails to improve downstream wall clock, or if any correctness, support-decision, explicit-failure, tensor-state, artifact-identity, or zero-fallback check regresses.
final_candidate.compute_budget: Approximately 0.2 GPU-day + $0 API; the main cost is one U280 for roughly 6-8 weeks of wrapper/runtime development and about 7 board-days for signature regression, matched pp512/tg128 trials, fault injection, and controls, within the five-month envelope.

differentiation_from_lit.delta: It chooses backends from exact-shape and previous-backend features and sums measured operator/transition costs in replay, whereas this candidate constructs a live no-fallback receipt/version protocol that reduces actual XRT starts and waits while committing the connected GGML graph's outputs and state.

Its host agent may choose CPU execution and retrieves FPGA outputs before subsequent progress, whereas this candidate fixes every admitted node to its pinned FPGA artifact and permits deferred visibility only through version-gated execution and atomic state commit.

ATLAS generates model hardware through a universal GEMM frontend and architecture-aware RTL backend, whereas this candidate leaves the irregular real GGML graph and its 11 replaceable operator families intact and changes only their strict admission-to-launch-and-commit contract.

final_candidate.what_step_was_missed: It would have needed to replace replay with an integrated framework transaction that binds each support decision to a concrete artifact, carries tensor and mutable-state versions across asynchronous FPGA runs, and commits the real autoregressive graph only after live execution succeeds.
